brief: The Market Ear reports Nasdaq futures positioning has snapped back sharply. Non-dealer net exposure bought every week from August 4 through September 1, a record $51.3bn in notional terms (per Quinn, GS). Hedge funds led the buying with $37.5bn net, almost entirely short covering ($38.6bn), so the note argues near-term Nasdaq strength reflects short covering rather than fresh aggressive longs. That leaves futures positioning relatively elevated heading into a packed micro and macro calendar. Separately, the note flags that put exposure has collapsed as shorts were covered, stripping out downside protection at the same time (GS charts). SPX skew has collapsed too (MS): investors hold fewer puts and pay considerably less for downside protection, and a Nomura chart shows the downside fear premium has been washed out. The note does not issue a forward price call.
